source.author: lucan
source.text: Ultro acies inferre parant: armisque coruscas Nocturni texere faces: audaxque iuventus Erupit: non hasta viris, non letifer arcus, Telum flamma fuit, rapiensque incendia ventus Per Romana tulit celeri munimina cursu.
source.text_original: Ultro acies inferre parant: armisque coruscas / Nocturni texere faces: audaxque iuventus / Erupit: non hasta viris, non letifer arcus, / Telum flamma fuit, rapiensque incendia ventus / Per Romana tulit celeri munimina cursu.
source.text_english: They prepare of their own accord to bring the battle on: and the torches of night, flashing among their arms, were covered over; and the bold youth burst forth. For the men there was no spear, no death-bringing bow; fire was their weapon, and the wind, snatching up the flames, carried them in swift course through the Roman fortifications.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: qui tum Minyis trepidantibus horror, cum picei fulsere poli pavidamque coruscae ante ratem cecidere faces, antemnaque laevo prona dehiscentem cornu cum sustulit undam.
reuse.text_original: qui tum Minyis trepidantibus horror, / cum picei fulsere poli pavidamque coruscae / ante ratem cecidere faces, antemnaque laevo / prona dehiscentem cornu cum sustulit undam.
reuse.text_english: Then there was dread among the Minyae, when the pitch-dark heavens flashed and the blazing brands fell before the terrified ship, and the leaning yardarm lifted the wave breaking open on the left side.
